record.original_question: Can it be proved rigorously that the total number of geodetic graphs of diameter d >= 2 that are homeomorphic to the Petersen graph is (d + 3)C5, meaning the number of combinations of d + 3 elements taken 5 at a time?

evidence.quote: 1. Can be proved rigorously that the general number of all geodetic graphs of diameter d  2 homeomorphic to the Petersen graph is (d + 3)C5 (the number of combinations of d + 3 elements taken 5 at the time)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graph $G$ is called geodetic if between every pair of vertices of $G$ there is a unique shortest path. Two graphs are homeomorphic if both can be obtained from a common graph by subdividing edges (i.e., inserting degree-2 vertices into edges). The Petersen graph $P$ is the 3-regular graph on 10 vertices whose vertices are the 2-element subsets of $\{1,2,3,4,5\}$, with two vertices adjacent iff the corresponding subsets are disjoint.

For an integer $d \geq 2$, let $N(d)$ denote the number of (pairwise non-isomorphic) geodetic graphs of diameter $d$ that are homeomorphic to the Petersen graph $P$.

Prove or disprove rigorously the formula
$$N(d) \;=\; \binom{d+3}{5}$$
for every integer $d \geq 2$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjectured count $\binom{d+3}{5}$ for the number of geodetic graphs of diameter $d\ge 2$ homeomorphic to the Petersen graph appears as an explicit open question in work on enumeration of geodetic graphs homeomorphic to a given geodetic graph. Available sources describe an algorithmic enumeration and tabulate values for small diameters (d = 2..7), but no rigorous proof of the general closed form is reported.

status_evidence.title: Geodetic Graphs Homeomorphic to a Given Geodetic Graph
status_evidence.snippet: Enumeration of geodetic graphs homeomorphic to the Petersen graph for diameters 2 through 7 is carried out via an algorithmic procedure for solving an associated system of Diophantine equations.
status_evidence.claim: The enumeration is conducted algorithmically for small diameters; no general closed-form proof is established.

status_evidence.title: The Open Problem of Finding a General Classification of Geodetic Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Classification and enumeration of geodetic graphs remains open in general.
status_evidence.claim: General classification/enumeration of geodetic graphs is an open problem.
